summary: Martin Riesebrodt (1948–2014) worked in religious studies. He studied at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (Promotion), and Munich (Habilitation). He was a professor at the University of Chicago and its Divinity School (1990–2011) and at the Graduate Institute (2013).

Martin Seeger works in Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg by 2004 under Barend Jan Terwiel, where he held an attested post in 2004, and is a Council member of the Pali Text Society.

Martin Straube works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, his posts include Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeit at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Research Fellow at IIBS, Foreign Adjunct Professor at Pune University, and Honorary Research Associate at Bristol.

Martin T. Adam works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes, also studying at CIHTS and under various teachers. He has served as an instructor at McGill University.

Martin Willson (d. 2005) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Lambert Schmithausen and received her doctorate from the University of Vienna, where she has also held a post as a researcher.
Martine Kropman is an Indologist. She has been a PhD researcher at the University of Groningen and an external PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.
Martino Dibeltulo works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under the supervision of Donald S. Lopez Jr., and was mentored by Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was an art historian. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and held a post at the University of Michigan from circa 1949 to 1983.
Mary Anne Cartelli works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Philip B. Yampolsky.

Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) worked in Sinology and history. She studied at Vassar College and Radcliffe College (MA, PhD). She was curator at the Hoover Institution (~1946–1959) and held professorships at Stanford (1947) and Yale (1959, 1964).

Mary Evelyn Tucker (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. She studied at SUNY Fredonia, Sophia, Fordham, and Columbia (PhD). She served as Professor of Religion at Bucknell (~1989–2006) before becoming a professor at Yale (~2006).

Mary Haas (1910–1996) was a linguist. She studied at Earlham College, the University of Chicago, and Yale University, working under Edward Sapir (~1930–1935). She held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1948 to 1977.
Mary Jaksch (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey and also studied under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Margaret McCabe (b. 1948) is a philosopher. She studied at Newnham College (BA) and Cambridge (PhD). She was a Fellow at Murray Edwards College (1981–1990) and Professor at King's College London (1990–2014).

Mary Shepherd Slusser (1918–2017) was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist. She studied at Michigan, Columbia (PhD), NYU, and Harvard. She worked for the US State Department (1951–1958) and the National Museum of African Art (1971–1978).
Marybeth White works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned a double major honors degree from York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University.
Maryla Falk (1906–1980) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She held a post at the University of Warsaw from circa 1934 to 1939.
Marylin Martin Rhie works in Buddhist studies, art history, and Sinology. She studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, and has served as a professor at Smith College.

Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned three degrees including a doctorate from Kyoto University, where he was a professor (1981–1993), before serving as professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).
